title: Unbounded input via gets() — review required
description: gets() reads a line into a buffer with no length limit, so any long input overflows the buffer. gets() cannot be used safely and was removed from the C standard. This rule flags every use; there is no safe case to allowlist.
remediation: Delete gets(): use fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin) and strip the newline, or getline() for dynamic input. Re-audit callers for truncation handling.
limitation: Lexical: matches gets( exactly, so fgets( and similar safe names never match. Buffer-size reasoning for the replacement is out of scope.

tests.line: // banned: gets has no length check
